Cairo.text: Egypt's capital was founded in 969 and became the seat of the Fatimid Caliphate in 973.
Cairo.evidence: Thereafter, Cairo was founded in 969, and became the official seat and capital of the Fatimid Caliphate in 973.

Lagos.text: Nigeria's Lagos hosts the Dangote Refinery, set to be the world's largest oil refinery once expanded.
Lagos.evidence: The employer with the most staff is the Dangote Refinery, which, once expanded, will be the world's largest oil refinery.

Kinshasa.text: Called Léopoldville until 1966, the DR Congo's capital is the most populous city proper outside China.
Kinshasa.evidence: Kinshasa ..., formerly named Léopoldville (Dutch: Leopoldstad) from 1881 to 1966, is the capital and largest city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. ... the world's seventh-most populous city proper (the most populous outside of China)

Nairobi.text: Kenya's capital is the only capital city in the world with a national park inside its boundaries.
Nairobi.evidence: Nicknamed the "Green City under the Sun", Nairobi is uniquely notable for being the only capital city in the world that hosts a national park within its boundaries.

Johannesburg.text: South Africa's largest city was founded in 1886, after gold was found on what was farmland.
Johannesburg.evidence: Johannesburg was established in 1886, following the discovery of gold, on what was once farmland.

Luanda.text: Angola's capital is the most populous Portuguese-speaking capital city in the world.
Luanda.evidence: Luanda and its metropolitan area is the most populous Portuguese-speaking national capital in the world and the most populous Lusophone city outside Brazil.

Khartoum.text: Sudan's capital sits where the White Nile and the Blue Nile meet.
Khartoum.evidence: Khartoum is located at the confluence of the White Nile – flowing north from Lake Victoria – and the Blue Nile, flowing west from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.

Abidjan.text: Legend says Ivory Coast's Abidjan is named after a misheard cry: "I just cut the leaves."
Abidjan.evidence: Terrified by this unexpected meeting, he fled shouting "min-chan m'bidjan", which means in the Ebrié language: "I just cut the leaves." The explorer, thinking that his question had been answered, recorded the name of the locale as Abidjan.

Accra.text: Ghana's capital is named after soldier ants, a name Twi speakers gave the town and its people.
Accra.evidence: The name specifically refers to soldier ants, and was applied to the town and people by the Twi speakers.

Dar es Salaam.text: Tanzania's largest city takes its name from the Arabic for "Abode of Peace".
Dar es Salaam.evidence: Dar es Salaam (... from Arabic: دَار السَّلَام, romanised: Dār as-Salām, lit. 'Abode of Peace') is the largest city and financial hub of Tanzania
